target: Calegari Question 7.3, attributed to Dunfield: an algorithm for boundary slopes of essential laminations carried by the branched two-skeleton of a fixed taut ideal triangulation, with the exact boundary convention and output language still to be specified.
accepted_conclusions: Theorem 1: exact decision for finite rational-affine point constraints on shared increasing interval homeomorphisms, with rational parameters and rational PL witnesses.
Corollary 2 and Section 4: compatibility of supplied regular finite boundary itinerary diagrams and exact finite homology output at a supplied total-length bound.
Proposition 3: finite periodic point samples do not enforce all-boundary-leaves-closed behavior, even within rational PL maps when samples are rational.
Theorem 4: exact full return-identity decision for a supplied rational PL suspension lift with supplied section, peripheral basis, chosen lift and primitive slope pair p,q with q>0.
Authored shared-map obstruction and precise source peripheral-basis comparison, with all geometric and boundary-condition qualifications.
geometric_essentiality: Conditional. Global embedded proper realization, full carrying with the stated essentiality criterion, and the chosen global boundary condition must be separately established.
remaining_gap: Fix the target boundary convention and effective output language; prove global realization and completeness for all admitted laminations carried by the original fixed carrier, including non-full and nongeneric cases where admitted; and obtain a terminating treatment of unbounded or infinite holonomy and global peripheral constraints. Closed-boundary realization needs a functional identity beyond finitely many point evaluations. A real-slope convention additionally needs a full-set representation and effective endpoint/infinite-orbit control.
supplied_global_return_map_scope: Theorem 4 does not extract a suspension model or find a compatible global map. The section and basis fix the meaning of p,q; q=0 is outside the model, a lift change shifts p by kq, and rejection concerns only the supplied map.
